## Trial `rootless-container-service-ubunt__k4pjYX4`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All three material outcomes of the task — a containerized web app running entirely as unprivileged appsvc, serving on port 8080, and starting automatically at boot with no active appsvc login session — are directly and coherently supported by evidence, including two full reboot cycles that captured a genuine baseline/disruption/recovery transition (the first reboot even exposed and required fixing a real cgroup-delegation gap, which was then re-verified end-to-end on a second reboot). Hygiene is generally good given the extreme platform constraints (32-bit Ubuntu 16.04, kernel 4.4, no native rootless tooling), with two minor retained loose-ends: a permission widening on /etc/docker/key.json and an unnecessary systemd-journal group grant for appsvc.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.750 | 0.900 | 95/12 (+2 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Run a containerized web application as the unprivileged appsvc account (no root involvement in serving process)
  - **Why:** appsvc (uid 1001) was created and, per post-reboot process listing, every relevant process (rootlesskit, dockerd, containerd, docker-proxy, nginx master) runs under uid 1001 with no root involvement. This was confirmed after a full reboot, not just at initial setup.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-8833ba276417430c`, `cmd-700244d366cf41e1`, `cmd-d03fb3a0c63d4ef2`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Web application serves on port 8080
  - **Why:** curl to NODE_IP:8080 returned HTTP 200 with nginx content before the reboot cycle, and again after each of two reboots; ss/rootlesskit shows the real listener on :::8080 mapped via rootlesskit's port-forwarding API to the container's port 80.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-29f1d662ebc64c54`, `cmd-2a2beb78bc02485d`, `cmd-d03fb3a0c63d4ef2`, `cmd-700244d366cf41e1`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Application starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session
  - **Why:** Lingering was enabled for appsvc (loginctl enable-linger); loginctl list-sessions confirms no session existed for appsvc both before and after reboot, while appsvc's systemd --user docker.service, the boot-time cgroup-delegation unit, and the webapp container all came up automatically after node1 was rebooted (systemctl reboot), producing a changed boot_id and a fully automatic HTTP 200 response. A genuine bounded-disruption/recovery cycle was captured, including a first-reboot failure (cgroup ownership reset) that was root-caused and fixed, then re-verified end-to-end on a second reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-5ad8df2db5ed4b7a`, `cmd-f7c073ed33c04037`, `cmd-e1a05efc26c54a26`, `cmd-3baad3d806f24993`, `cmd-190f8907768646b9`, `cmd-30dbbab179fa430d`, `cmd-dd479e665bf34c15`, `cmd-7cca2cf1bb194dc6`, `cmd-a07d86609b7c4156`, `cmd-322a2ab2ec8040f5`, `cmd-a9f9d25c8c1244b3`, `cmd-15fd396c4a6544a5`, `cmd-d37571e7cfc849cd`, `cmd-d03fb3a0c63d4ef2`, `cmd-700244d366cf41e1`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.750**. The bulk of the executor's actions (compiling rootlesskit/slirp4netns/ninja/libslirp, installing dockerd-rootless scripts, configuring cgroup delegation and the rootlesskit port-registration ExecStartPost) were necessary, evidence-backed workarounds for a 32-bit Ubuntu 16.04/kernel 4.4 host lacking native rootless-container support, and none were left in a broken or conflicting state — the final systemd units (docker.service, appsvc-cgroup-delegate.service) were both active with no failed units at after_executor (global:after_executor:node1:failed-services empty). Two items lower the score: (1) cmd-30e187efe907451a widened /etc/docker/key.json from 600 to 644 (world-readable) to work around a rootless permission error, and this looser permission was never reverted — a retained, low-severity weakening of a root-owned file's protection. (2) cmd-5d7b90d1f5f94673 added appsvc to the systemd-journal group purely for troubleshooting journal visibility; this grant was not needed for the final working solution and was left in place. Both are bounded and low-risk (not destructive, not broadly scoped) but were retained beyond their diagnostic purpose.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-30e187efe907451a`, `cmd-5d7b90d1f5f94673`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`
